newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: 20 missing as landslide hits Australian ski town.
newsitem.headline: 20 missing as landslide hits Australian ski town.

text.p: Up to 20 people were missing on Thursday after a landslide demolished two lodges at Australia's busiest ski resort, injuring many people.
Police said they expected fatalities, although witnesses reported hearing voices from the rubble.

Rescuers working in sub-zero temperatures were unable to begin searching the wreckage at the Thredbo Alpine Village, in the Snowy Mountains about 150 km (90 miles) southwest of Canberra, because the site remained dangerously unstable.

"There are early suggestions that we have about 18-20 people that have not been accounted for," a police spokesman said from Sydney. "The site instability is hampering the rescue operation ... it's very unstable unfortunately."
Local police said it appeared several dozen people had been injured but the exact number and the extent of their injuries was not known.
There were early media reports that some people had been killed. Police could not confirm this, although one senior officer said it was almost certain that people had died.

"At this point in time it is my belief that it's highly likely that we will have a number of fatalities," Superintendent Charlie Sanderson told reporters in the mountain town of Jindabyne, about 35 km (20 miles) from the scene.
Sanderson said snow expected in the area later on Thursday could further hamper rescue operations.
Tourists from nearby lodges said they head voices crying from the rubble as they tried to find survivors before police halted rescue efforts over safety concerns.
"We got down into the rubble as soon as we'd evacuated families and children," said television journalist Glenn Milne, who was holidaying at Thredbo.
"We heard three voices, three separate voices," he said.
"When the rescue services arrived, they judged the situation simply to be too dangerous and told us we had to get out of there," he said.
The landslide occurred just before midnight on Wednesday at a time when Thredbo is packed with thousands of Australian and foreign visitors at the height of Australia's skiing season.
Police set up roadblocks at Jindabyne to block access to the resort as engineers, geologists and mine rescue experts arrived to assess the situation.
Witnesses said the scene was a jumble of debris and wreckage. They said earth slid about 100 metres (yards) down a hill, dumping one lodge on top of the second.
One of the lodges housed staff working at the village.
"It looks like someone has taken a great big bulldozer and just drove over both the lodges and they just slid down the hill," one witness told Australian Broadcasting Corporation radio.

"There is really nothing left of them but bits and pieces," he said. "It reminds me of looking at a picture of a tornado site or something where it's just cleaned a path through and on either side there is no damage whatsoever."
Rescuers and ambulances, including air ambulances, were rushing to the scene from as far away as Sydney, a five to six hour drive in normal conditions.
Rescue officials said they were unable to get helicopters into the area because of the icy conditions.
